space_radiation.label: Space radiation
space_radiation.summary: Outside Earth's protective magnetic field, radiation levels are higher. Over time this raises health risks.

isolation_confinement.label: Isolation and confinement
isolation_confinement.summary: Being in a small crew, far from family and friends, for a long time affects mood, sleep and focus.

distance_from_earth.label: Distance from Earth
distance_from_earth.summary: The farther from Earth, the longer a message takes to arrive. The crew must be ready to act alone until Earth replies.

gravity_fields.label: Gravity fields (including microgravity)
gravity_fields.summary: Little or no gravity lets bones and muscles weaken, and changes where blood pressure sits in the body.

hostile_environment.label: Hostile closed environment
hostile_environment.summary: A sealed habitat changes air, noise, temperature and light compared to Earth, and can affect sleep and immunity.

brain.label: Brain
brain.what_it_does: Controls thinking, mood, sleep and reaction speed.
brain.space_effects: Isolation, confinement and disrupted schedules can affect mood, sleep quality and how fast you react.
brain.what_to_do: Keep a steady sleep schedule, do the daily mood check, and try a breathing exercise if you feel stressed.

eyes.label: Eyes
eyes.what_it_does: Vision, including pressure-sensitive structures at the back of the eye.
eyes.space_effects: Fluid shifts in microgravity can raise pressure around the eyes and blur vision over time.
eyes.what_to_do: Report any blurry vision right away; it is treated as a red-flag symptom.

heart.label: Heart
heart.what_it_does: Pumps blood around the body; its workload and blood pressure change in microgravity.
heart.space_effects: Without gravity pulling blood down, more fluid sits near the chest and head, changing heart rate and blood pressure patterns.
heart.what_to_do: Keep up cardio exercise and log your heart rate and blood pressure each check.

stomach.label: Stomach and nutrition
stomach.space_effects: Appetite and taste can change in space, and it is easy to under-eat or under-drink without noticing.
stomach.what_to_do: Log every meal and your water intake; aim for the daily water target.

skeleton.label: Skeleton
skeleton.space_effects: Bones lose density in microgravity because they are not carrying weight like they do on Earth.
skeleton.what_to_do: Resistance exercise and enough calcium in meals help slow bone loss.

muscles.label: Muscles
muscles.space_effects: Muscles weaken quickly without gravity to work against, especially in the legs and back.
muscles.what_to_do: Daily resistance and cardio exercise is the main defense.

immune.label: Immune system
immune.what_it_does: Fights infection and manages inflammation; shown here as a whole-body glow.
immune.space_effects: Radiation and a sealed, recycled-air habitat can both affect immune function and body temperature regulation.
immune.what_to_do: Report fever or feeling unwell early; keep the habitat clean and follow hygiene routines.

heart_rate.title: How to measure heart rate
steps: Sit still for 2 minutes before measuring.
Use the cuff or sensor as shown in the kit.
Enter the number on the Live tab.

blood_pressure.title: How to measure blood pressure
steps: Sit with your arm resting at heart height.
Wrap the cuff snugly above the elbow.
Stay still and quiet while it measures.
Enter both numbers: systolic (top) and diastolic (bottom).

blood_sugar.title: How to measure blood sugar
steps: Measure fasting, before your first meal if possible.

temperature.title: How to measure temperature
steps: Use the thermometer as shown in the kit.
Wait for the reading to settle.

learn_cards.title: The five hazards of spaceflight
learn_cards.body: Space radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, gravity fields, and a hostile closed environment all affect crew health in different ways.

learn_cards.title: Why we check every day
learn_cards.body: Small changes build up slowly in space. Daily checks catch problems early, before they become emergencies.

learn_cards.title: GREEN, YELLOW, RED
learn_cards.body: GREEN means normal. YELLOW means pay attention and take the suggested action. RED means act now and the flight surgeon is alerted.

learn_cards.title: When to call the flight surgeon
learn_cards.body: Call for any RED result, or any YELLOW that does not improve after you follow the advice.
